sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)
📰 News (NYT / WSJ / Bloomberg / FT / Washington Post / Economist)

items.title: Cracks Grow Across the AI Trade as Memory-Chip Stocks Tumble
items.desc: Memory-chip makers led a sharp slide in AI-linked stocks, with Korean and Japanese chip names hit hard amid doubts about AI spending and a reported Chinese DRAM breakthrough claim. [Bloomberg, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Hyperscaler Debt Binge Risks Curbing Access for Emerging Nations
items.desc: Bloomberg reports on the risk that heavy bond issuance by AI hyperscalers could crowd emerging-market borrowers out of global debt markets. [Bloomberg, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Infosys Chairman Calls Job Fears ‘Hogwash’ as AI Spurs Business
items.desc: Infosys's chairman dismisses worries that AI will destroy jobs, arguing that AI is generating new business for the IT-services firm. [Bloomberg, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Chip stocks slide in wake of ‘casino’ comment by Broadcom boss
items.desc: Semiconductor shares fell after Broadcom's chief executive likened much AI investor behavior to gambling, feeding wider concern about sentiment and financing discipline in the AI trade. [Financial Times, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: IMF upgrades outlook for UK as AI drives growth spurt
items.desc: The IMF raised its UK growth forecast, crediting AI-related investment and exports; it puts 2026 growth at about 1.3% and sees a slight slowdown in 2027. [Financial Times, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: China resorts to Nvidia gaming chips in search for AI firepower
items.desc: The FT reports that Chinese AI developers are turning to Nvidia gaming chips to get compute amid supply constraints on advanced AI processors. [Financial Times, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Will Accenture survive or thrive in the age of AI?
items.desc: The FT asks whether the consulting and IT-services giant can adapt its business model as AI reshapes the demand for outsourced services. [Financial Times, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Chip Stocks Tumble on A.I. Spending Fears and Rising Chinese Competition
items.desc: The New York Times reports a tumble in chip stocks as investors worry about the durability of AI spending and growing competition from Chinese chipmakers. [NYT, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: ‘Phantom’ Data Centers Are Demanding More From the Power Grid Than They Need
items.desc: The Wall Street Journal reports that speculative data-center requests are inflating power-grid demand forecasts, and utilities are tightening terms to separate real projects from phantom ones. [WSJ, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: Nasdaq Futures Fall as Global AI Selloff Intensifies
items.desc: Nasdaq futures dropped as a selloff in AI-related stocks spread across global markets. [WSJ, published 2026-10-13]

items.title: How the AI Boom Is Fueling Global Financial Risks
items.desc: Bloomberg examines how a circular funding model, with foreign money flowing into data-center buildouts, is accelerating the AI boom while amplifying financial imbalances that recall the run-up to the global financial crisis. Related IMF analysis counts about $300 billion of equity and $650 billion of debt moving into weaker AI firms through disclosed deals since 2023. [Bloomberg, published 2026-10-12]

items.title: Meta Says New AI Model Is State-of-the-Art, Will Make Muse Agent Smarter
items.desc: Meta unveiled new AI models that it calls state-of-the-art and says will improve its Muse agent; Meta's stock rose on the news. [WSJ, published 2026-10-12]

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Hello and welcome to the AI Research Digest briefing for October thirteenth, twenty twenty-six. No new papers cleared our filters today, so this is a news day, and the theme is nerves in the AI trade.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: I'm Sam. Right, the big story is a global slide in chip stocks. The New York Times and Bloomberg both report memory-chip makers tumbling, on fears about AI spending and competition from China.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: The Financial Times adds the trigger that got a lot of attention: Broadcom's chief executive compared much AI investor behavior to gambling. Chip shares slid after that.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Bloomberg also describes a reported Chinese breakthrough claim in memory chips, which hit Korean and Japanese names especially hard. Chinese chip claims have been walked back before, so that part is worth treating carefully.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: And the Wall Street Journal says Nasdaq futures fell as the selloff in AI stocks intensified globally.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Underneath the price moves is a structural worry. A Bloomberg feature this week looks at how a circular funding model, where foreign money flows into data-center buildouts, is speeding up the boom while amplifying imbalances.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Related IMF analysis counts about three hundred billion dollars of equity and six hundred fifty billion dollars of debt moving into weaker AI firms through disclosed deals since twenty twenty-three.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Another Bloomberg story asks what happens when hyperscalers issue so much debt that emerging-market borrowers get crowded out of global bond markets.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: On the physical side, the Wall Street Journal reports on phantom data centers. Speculative projects are requesting more grid power than they will ever need, which inflates demand forecasts.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Utilities are responding by tightening terms to tell real projects from speculative ones. That matters for anyone who pays an electricity bill.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Not everything is gloomy. The FT says the IMF upgraded its outlook for the United Kingdom, crediting AI-related investment and exports, with growth around one point three percent this year.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And at Infosys, the chairman called job-loss fears hogwash, saying AI is actually bringing the company new business. The FT, meanwhile, asks whether Accenture can survive or thrive in the age of AI.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Two more items. The FT reports Chinese developers are turning to Nvidia gaming chips for compute. And Meta unveiled new models it calls state-of-the-art, which sent its stock up.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: So the picture is a boom with real money behind it, but with investors increasingly asking who is financing it and whether the demand is real.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: That's all for today. Full summaries and links are in the web archive.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Thanks for listening, and we'll be back with the next digest.

footnote: Window: 2026-10-12 (last run) → 2026-10-13. All sources were reachable this run. arXiv, INFORMS and NBER had no new matching AI-focused papers; SSRN searches turned up no papers with a verified in-window posting date. News summaries are based on feed headlines plus web searches.
